earlier_scan.source_named: Schaefer, Paul & Jennifer Schaefer 2003. Collected field reports on the phonology of Safaliba (IAS Legon); Bodua-Mango 2012 NTNU thesis read online - no word-stress statement

sources.citation: Naden, Tony (comp; original data from Paul Schaefer, with material from T. Naden and W.A.A. Wilson). 2024. A preliminary dictionary of the Safaliba language of northern Ghana. GILLBT / Aardvarks Lexico. 36 pp.
sources.note: Lexical; introduction covers vowel inventory/alphabetisation only; no prosody. Bibliography confirms Schaefer & Schaefer 'Collected field reports on the phonology of Safaliba' (IAS Legon) as the phonology source.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Paul Alan. 2009. Narrative storyline marking in Safaliba: determining the meaning and discourse function of a typologically-suspect pronoun set. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. xvi+350 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Ch.2 'Phonology overview' (pp.70-77) and sec. 2.3 'Tone and Intonation' (pp.88-95): two-level tone system (H/L) with automatic and non-automatic downstep, TBU = mora, tone melodies, lexical tone on nouns and grammatical tone on verbs; sentence pitch contour determined by word tones. No statement anywhere about word stress or accent (the only 'stress/prominence' mentions are in the theoretical discussion of focus in English/Dik).
Safaliba mentioned only in classification (3 hits); nothing on Safaliba prosody.

sources.citation: Bodua-Mango, R. K. 2015. The phonology of a three year old Safaliba-speaking child. MPhil thesis, University of Ghana, Legon. 122 pp.
sources.note: Ch.3 gives adult Safaliba segmental phonology and syllable structure (following Schaefer & Schaefer 2003); tone mentioned only in a note on vowel-length pairs (p.51) and as future work (p.93). No statement on stress.

sources.citation: Bodua-Mango, Kenneth. 2012. Coordinators in Safaliba. MA thesis, Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), Trondheim. 115 pp.
sources.note: Syntax/pragmatics of coordinators; only notes that 'Basic rising and falling tone was also annotated' (p.4). Nothing on stress.

sources.note: Content unseen (unpublished GILLBT ms, not online). Schaefer 2009 lists it in his references (p. 343) and cites it once, in footnote 28 to sec. 2.1.1 (pp. 73-74), crediting 'Samuel Issah (ms, p.c.)' for arguing the phonemic status of Safaliba's marginal tenth vowel (the +ATR low central vowel that triggers +ATR suffix harmony) - a segmental/ATR point. Schaefer's tone section (2.3, pp. 88-95) does not cite it. Whether the ms treats tonal processes is unknown; title only.
